construction_markdown:
No new leaderboard code is claimed. Consider the explicit field

\[
F=\mathbb F_2[\alpha]/(\alpha^{16}+\alpha^5+\alpha^3+\alpha^2+1)
\]

and the sets

\[
A=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F_2}\{1,\alpha,\ldots,\alpha^{14}\},\qquad Y=\mathbb F_2^{15}.
\]

For `z=Σ_{i=0}^{15}z_i α^i`, define the affine-Hadamard block

\[
H(z)_y=z_0+\sum_{i=1}^{15}z_i y_i.
\]

Let

\[
D_0=\{(f(a))_{a\in A}:f\in F[X],\ \deg f\le64\}.
\]

Then `H^A(D_0)` is the durable `[2^30,1040,535822336]_2` construction. The result audits every binary-additive outer supercode `D` with `D_0⊆D⊆F^A`, retaining exactly this coordinatewise inner map.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Let `F` have characteristic two, `A⊂F`, and `D_m` be evaluation of degree-at-most-`m` polynomials on `A`. If `v∉D_m` and every word in `v+D_m` satisfies `N_0-N_1≤m`, then for every `m`-set `R⊂A`, with `G_R(X)=∏_{r∈R}(X-r)`, one necessarily has `Σ_{x∈A\R}G_R(x)^{-1}=0`. Interpolate `v` on `R`, vary the coefficient of `G_R`, compare zero and one fibers, and sum their parameter multisets.

The subspace-polynomial calculation gives `Σ_{x∈A\R}1/G_R(x)=0x0990≠0`. distance_audit: For any `u∈F^A`, `wt(H^A(u))=2^14(32768-N_0(u)+N_1(u))`. Thus the immutable target is exactly `N_0(u)-N_1(u)≤64`.
The base space `D_0` satisfies the target: a nonconstant degree-at-most-64 polynomial has at most 64 zero evaluations, while nonzero constants have no zero evaluations.
For `v∉D_0`, every interpolated coset word `u_t` is nonzero, so the assumed minimum-distance condition applies to every `t∈F`.
The 64 forced zeros give `z_t≤o_t`; summing over all `t` gives equal totals, hence `z_t=o_t` for every `t`.
The resulting necessary reciprocal sum is explicitly `0x0990`, contradicting the required value zero.
explicitness_audit: Field elements are 16-bit polynomial-basis words; multiplication is reduction modulo bitmask `0x1002d`.
The evaluation space, inner coordinates, subspace `U`, element `b=0x0040`, and set `R={0x0001,…,0x0040}` are completely fixed.
The subspace polynomial is reproducible from a six-step recurrence with the displayed `β_i`; no search or random choice enters the proof.
Independent direct enumeration of the original 32,704 reciprocal terms returned `0x0990`, matching the symbolic coset calculation.
The theorem only excludes outer additive extensions containing `D_0` and using the same coordinatewise `H`; it does not exclude unrelated binary extensions or different inner maps.

proof_markdown:
## Theorem

Let `D⊆F^A` be an `F_2`-linear space containing `D_0`. If every nonzero word of `H^A(D)` has weight at least `535,822,336`, then `D=D_0`. Thus the shared dimension-1040 code admits no strict binary-additive outer extension using the same coordinatewise affine-Hadamard encoder.

## 1. Field and base code

Put

\[
p(Z)=Z^{16}+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1.
\]

Direct repeated squaring modulo `p` gives

\[
Z^{256}\equiv Z^8+Z^7+Z^3+Z,\qquad Z^{65536}\equiv Z.
\]

Writing `h=Z^8+Z^7+Z^3`, direct Euclidean division gives

\[
p=(Z^8+Z^7+Z^6+Z^5+Z^4+Z^2+1)h+(Z^2+1),
\]

\[
h=(Z^6+Z^5+Z^4+Z^3+Z^2+1)(Z^2+1)+1.
\]

Hence `gcd(p,Z^256+Z)=1`; Rabin's degree-16 criterion proves that `p` is irreducible.

The evaluation map defining `D_0` is injective because a nonzero degree-at-most-64 polynomial cannot vanish at all 32,768 points of `A`. Therefore `dim_{F_2}D_0=16·65=1040`.

For `u∈F^A`, let `N_c(u)=|{a:u_a=c}|`. Character orthogonality for the affine block gives weight zero at symbol `0`, weight `2^15` at symbol `1`, and weight `2^14` at every other symbol. Consequently

\[
\operatorname{wt}(H^A(u))=2^{14}(32768-N_0(u)+N_1(u)).
\]

Since the target equals `(32768-64)2^14`, it is equivalent to

\[
N_0(u)-N_1(u)\le64. \tag{1}
\]

This proves the lower bound for `D_0`. It is attained by choosing 64 roots and scaling their product so that none of its remaining values equals 1, as `32704<|F^*|=65535`.

## 2. Reciprocal-sum extension lemma

Assume toward contradiction that `v∈D\D_0`. Fix any 64-set `R⊂A`. Let `h_R` be the unique polynomial of degree at most 63 satisfying `h_R(r)=v_r` for `r∈R`, and put

\[
G_R(X)=\prod_{r\in R}(X-r).
\]

For every `t∈F`, define

\[
u_t=v+\operatorname{ev}_A(h_R+tG_R).
\]

Then `u_t∈D`, all its coordinates in `R` vanish, and `u_t≠0`; otherwise `v∈D_0`. Let `z_t` and `o_t` count its additional zeros and its ones outside `R`. Applying (1) gives

\[
64+z_t-o_t\le64,
\]

so `z_t≤o_t`.

For each fixed `x∈A\R`, the map

\[
t\longmapsto v_x+h_R(x)+tG_R(x)
\]

is a bijection of `F`. Therefore, as `t` ranges over `F`, coordinate `x` contributes exactly once to the zero counts and once to the one counts. Hence

\[
\sum_tz_t=|A\setminus R|=\sum_to_t.
\]

Together with `z_t≤o_t`, this forces `z_t=o_t` for every `t`.

Set

\[
\rho_x=\frac{v_x+h_R(x)}{G_R(x)}.
\]

The zero-parameter multiset is `{ρ_x:x∈A\R}`, while the one-parameter multiset is `{ρ_x+G_R(x)^{-1}:x∈A\R}`. Their equality implies equality of their sums, and therefore

\[
\sum_{x\in A\setminus R}\frac1{G_R(x)}=0. \tag{2}
\]

Thus (2) is necessary for every 64-set `R`, independently of `v`.

## 3. An explicit violating set

Take

\[
U=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F_2}\{1,\alpha,\ldots,\alpha^5\},
\qquad b=\alpha^6,
\qquad R=(U\setminus\{0\})\cup\{b\}.
\]

Let

\[
L(X)=\prod_{u\in U}(X-u).
\]

A reproducible calculation begins with `L_0(X)=X` and, for `i=0,…,5`, uses

\[
\beta_i=L_i(\alpha^i),\qquad L_{i+1}(X)=L_i(X)^2+\beta_iL_i(X).
\]

Modulo bitmask `0x1002d`, the six values are

\[
(\beta_0,\ldots,\beta_5)=
(\mathtt{0001},\mathtt{0006},\mathtt{0168},\mathtt{47be},\mathtt{b444},\mathtt{4c35}),
\]

and

\[
L(X)=X^{64}+\mathtt{2e0c}X^{32}+\mathtt{71ee}X^{16}
+\mathtt{d9a4}X^8+\mathtt{2198}X^4
+\mathtt{c6ca}X^2+\mathtt{6115}X.
\]

Write `λ=0x6115`, `μ=0xc6ca`, and `B=L(b)=0xe9f1`. Since

\[
G_R(X)=\frac{L(X)}X(X-b),
\]

partition `A\R` into `0`, the nontrivial elements of `b+U`, and the remaining `U`-cosets. The first two parts contribute

\[
\frac1{\lambda b},
\qquad
\frac1B+\frac{b\mu}{\lambda B},
\]

using `Σ_{u∈U\{0}}u^{-1}=μ/λ`. On a remaining fiber `L(x)=y`, logarithmic differentiation of `L` gives contribution

\[
\frac{b\lambda}{y(y+B)}.
\]

The fibers pair under `y↦y+B`, so all these latter contributions cancel in characteristic two. Hence

\[
\sum_{x\in A\setminus R}\frac1{G_R(x)}
=
\frac{B+\lambda b+\mu b^2}{\lambda Bb}.
\]

Exact field arithmetic gives

\[
\lambda b=\mathtt{46f8},\qquad
\mu b^2=\mathtt{7311},
\]

\[
B+\lambda b+\mu b^2=\mathtt{dc18}\ne0,
\qquad
\lambda Bb=\mathtt{1d5c}.
\]

Therefore the reciprocal sum is `0x0990`, contradicting (2). This proves `D=D_0`.

## 4. Broader limited-independence certificate ceiling

Let an `r`-bit inner encoder consist of a spanning multiset `\mathcal L` of `B` nonzero linear functionals, and define

\[
W(z)=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal L}(-1)^{\ell(z)},
\qquad P_+=\sum_{W(z)>0}W(z).
\]

Because all functionals are nonzero, `Σ_zW(z)=0`. Fourier inversion at any occurring functional gives `Σ_z|W(z)|≥2^r`; moreover `W(0)=B`. Thus

\[
P_+\ge\max(B,2^{r-1}).
\]

For a nonconstant degree-at-most-`t` polynomial, each symbol fiber has size at most `t`, so the universal positive-part estimate is

\[
\sum_xW(f(x))\le tP_+.
\]

A proof relying solely on this estimate must demand `tP_+≤2^21`. Exact length `BN=2^30` and `N≤2^r` imply `B≥2^{30-r}`. Hence, for `t≥1`,

\[
k\le r\left(\left\lfloor
\frac{2^{21}}{\max(2^{30-r},2^{r-1})}
\right\rfloor+1\right).
\]

For `9≤r≤15` the maximum is 975 at `r=15`; for `16≤r≤22` the values begin `1040,561,306,171,100,63,44`. Thus this proof method has exact maximum 1040 at `r=16,t=64`. This final statement is only a certificate ceiling: special cancellations not captured by `tP_+` remain possible.

theorem_statement: Let `D_0⊂F_{2^16}^{32768}` be the degree-at-most-64 evaluation space underlying the durable dimension-1040 RS–affine code, and retain its coordinatewise affine-Hadamard inner encoder. If an `F_2`-linear outer space `D` contains `D_0` and every nonzero concatenated word has weight at least 535,822,336, then `D=D_0`. Hence this fixed-inner construction has no strict additive outer extension; this does not rule out unrelated binary codes or different inner maps.
title: Reciprocal-sum obstruction to additive extensions of the k=1040 RS–affine code
